title: Global functions on proper geometrically reduced connected algebraic spaces over fields
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $p:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be a proper algebraic space over $k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed. Suppose that for every algebraically closed field extension $\Omega/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], the algebraic space $Z_\Omega=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is reduced, nonempty and connected. An algebraically closed field is one in which every nonconstant polynomial has a root; reduced means that all the rings of affine etale scheme charts have no nonzero nilpotents. Connected means that the point space has no decomposition into two disjoint nonempty open subsets, with the point space and atlas topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Then the canonical structure homomorphism $k\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$, the global sections of $p^\sharp$ [def-sfb-space-module-structure-map] with $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}k,\mathcal O)=k$, is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras. Here $\mathcal O_Z$ is the structure sheaf on the small etale site, and $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ is its ring of global sections.

source.place: Tag 0DMY, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections, clause (7) and proof of clauses (4), (5), (7); geometric properties expressed by algebraically closed field tests

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/k$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and put $Z'=Z_\Omega$, $A=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ and $B=\Gamma(Z',\mathcal O_{Z'})$. Properness of $Z'\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ follows from the arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. The hypothesis on algebraically closed extensions says directly that $Z'$ is reduced, nonempty and connected. Therefore [lem-sfb-space-proper-connected-function-field], applied over $\Omega$, makes $B$ a field finite-dimensional over $\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 0DMY, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections, (1)--(3) applied after algebraic closure; proper base change: spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04WP, lemma-base-change-proper

proof.text: The structure homomorphism $v:\Omega\to B$ is bijective by [lem-pc-finite-extension-alg-closed]: its target is the finite field extension just obtained. In particular $B$ is a one-dimensional $\Omega$-vector space, with basis its unit. This applies to a reduced connected space, without any irreducibility assumption on $Z'$.

source.place: Tag 0DMY, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections, proof of (7), applied over the algebraically closed field

proof.text: Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $T'=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $g:T'\to T$. The map $g$ is flat by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat]; $p$ is quasi-compact and separated by properness. The structure module is quasi-coherent: locally its presentation is $0\to\mathcal O_Z\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_Z\to0$, as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Thus $N=p_*\mathcal O_Z$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-quasi-coherent-pushforward], and [lem-sfb-space-flat-direct-image-base-change] gives $g^*N\simeq p'_*\mathcal O_{Z'}$. Here the tensor pullback of the structure module is the structure module: locally $b\otimes a\mapsto b\,h^\sharp(a)$ has inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. The scheme Zariski/etale equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] preserves open sections and identifies tensor pullbacks. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], on the whole affine schemes $T,T'$, identifies the global sections of $g^*N$ with $A\otimes_k\Omega$. Evaluating the base-change isomorphism gives a bijective $\Omega$-linear map $\alpha:A\otimes_k\Omega\to B$. Its formula is $a\otimes c\mapsto h^*a\,v(c)$: the adjoint map in the cited base-change statement evaluates the pulled-back direct-image section by the counit, then multiplies by the tensor coefficient. In particular $\alpha(1\otimes c)=v(c)$. This is the actual structural comparison, with no arbitrary identification of the constants.

source.place: Tag 073K, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, i=0 and affine-base clause (2); spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03M9, lemma-pushforward; descent.tex Tags 03DX and 03LC; schemes.tex Tag 01I9, lemma-widetilde-pullback

proof.text: Since $\alpha(1\otimes1)=1_B\ne0$, the unit $1_A$ is nonzero. By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector] choose a $k$-basis of $A$ containing $1_A$. By the basis clause of [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], its tensors with $1$ form an $\Omega$-basis of $A\otimes_k\Omega$, hence their images under $\alpha$ form a basis of $B$. One of those images is $1_B$. There can be no second member: every $b\in B$ equals $v(c)1_B$ for some $c\in\Omega$ by step 2, giving a linear dependence with $1_B$. Thus the original basis is $\{1_A\}$. Every $a\in A$ is therefore $u(c)=c1_A$ for some $c\in k$, where $u$ is the structure map. If $u(c)=0$ and $c\ne0$, multiplication by $u(c^{-1})$ gives $1_A=0$, a contradiction. Hence $u$ is bijective. Its inverse preserves addition and multiplication by applying the injective ring map $u$ to each identity, so $u$ is the asserted isomorphism of $k$-algebras.
